The test image shows a corn stalk split open longitudinally. The internal pith is completely shredded/disintegrated with fibrous, pale gray-white tissue. This indicates a stalk rot disease. Key candidates: Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Gibberella_Disease, Fusarium_Disease.

Let me view reference images for the top candidates.
This Charcoal_Stalk_Rot reference is very close to the test image — shredded fibrous internal tissue, gray-white pith, split stalk. Let me check one more candidate.
Physoderma_Stalk_Rot shows dark spots on green stalk — not a match. I need one more reference view to reach 8.

This is a near-perfect match. Corn_Disease_32.jpg from Charcoal_Stalk_Rot shows the same dark blue background, same horizontal split stalk, same fibrous shredded internal pith, same pale gray-tan coloring. The test image is essentially identical in presentation.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: split corn stalk, completely shredded fibrous pith, pale gray-white, dark blue background
- Charcoal_Stalk_Rot ref (Corn_Disease_18, Corn_Disease_32): nearly identical — shredded fibrous stalk interior, same color, same presentation
- Diplodia_Stalk_Rot refs: showed external stalk views, not split interior
- Gibberella/Fusarium: ear rot, not stalk
- Physoderma_Stalk_Rot: black spots on green stalk, completely different
